activity.notes: ATLAS uses 37 BCE as a person-specific intellectual milestone because the Cambridge Ancient History dates Varro's publication of De re rustica to that year. This point represents a securely dated work and does not imply that his scholarly career was confined to 37 BCE.

sources.title: Agriculture (9c) — The Cambridge Ancient History
sources.citation_text: The Cambridge Ancient History states that Varro published De re rustica in 37 BCE at the end of a productive literary life.

sources.title: Varro, M. Terentius — Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology
sources.citation_text: The Perseus-hosted biographical entry identifies Marcus Terentius Varro, born in 116 BCE, as one of Rome's most learned and wide-ranging scholars and discusses De re rustica among his surviving works.
